cards.title: Missing a blanket of air

body.ages4To6: Mercury has almost no air to keep warmth in. Its nights can become very cold.

cards.title: Ice in a dark crater

body.ages10To12: Mercury’s low axial tilt lets some polar crater floors remain permanently shadowed. These cold traps can preserve water ice despite the planet’s sunlit heat.

deepDive.title: A model is a simplified question

body.ages4To6: Our tilted-globe model shows sunlight patterns. It does not tell us every detail of Uranus’s weather.
body.ages7To9: A sunlight model helps isolate tilt and orbital position. Winds, clouds, and the atmosphere make real weather more complex.
body.ages10To12: Qualitative illumination models are useful for causal comparison but do not predict measured temperatures or atmospheric circulation. A physical weather model needs additional variables and observations.

body.ages10To12: The term ice giant refers to a composition rich in substances historically classified as planetary ices. High interior pressure and temperature produce hot dense fluids.
